blocks.heading: What relative mass means
blocks.text: Chemical masses at this level are relative numbers. They compare an atom, molecule or formula unit with one twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom. Because both masses are divided by the same reference mass, relative masses have no unit. The carbon-12 reference gives chemists a consistent scale for atoms that are too small to weigh individually in grams.

blocks.heading: Four related quantities
blocks.text: Relative isotopic mass refers to one specified isotope. Carbon-13 therefore has a relative isotopic mass close to 13. Relative atomic mass, Ar, is different: it is the weighted mean for the naturally occurring isotopes of an element. Its value can therefore be non-integral. Relative molecular mass, Mr, adds the Ar values of all atoms in one molecule. For CO2, Mr = 12.0 + (2 × 16.0) = 44.0. Relative formula mass is found in the same way for substances described by formula units rather than separate molecules. For MgO it is 24.3 + 16.0 = 40.3. Calling this a molecular mass would wrongly imply that ionic magnesium oxide exists as separate MgO molecules.

blocks.heading: Choosing the correct mass
blocks.text: A sample contains chlorine atoms, Cl2 molecules and sodium chloride. Use relative atomic mass for one chlorine atom or for the average mass of chlorine atoms in nature. Use relative molecular mass for Cl2 because it consists of molecules: Mr = 2Ar(Cl). Use relative formula mass for NaCl because the formula represents the simplest ratio of ions in its lattice. The arithmetic is similar, but the name records what kind of chemical entity the formula represents.

blocks.heading: Where this leads
blocks.text: Relative masses become molar masses when expressed in g mol⁻¹. That connection is used throughout stoichiometry. Atomic structure in topic 1.2 explains isotopes more fully, while the ideal-gas topic 1.4 develops gas calculations beyond the fixed molar volumes used here.

blocks.heading: Consolidation and checks
blocks.text: A relative mass answers a comparison question, so it is written without g or kg. The numerical value becomes a molar mass when the quantity is one mole and the unit g mol⁻¹ is attached. For example, Ar(Na) is 23.0, while the molar mass of sodium is 23.0 g mol⁻¹. Keeping the quantity and unit separate prevents a relative-mass answer from being given a mass unit.
